title: ESA VALIDATION DATA CENTRE (EVDC) NOVA - EVOLUTION AND OPERATIONS - EXPRO+
description: The ESA atmospheric Validation Data Center (EVDC) provides centralized access to correlative Cal/Val data sets, such as Fiducial Reference Measurements (FRM), sondes, aircraft, and balloon campaigns. These are used to validate satellite-based atmospheric composition products. Since 2016, the EVDC has undergone significant modernization and evolution, introducing advanced functionalities and tools for the Cal/Val community, including an Orbit Prediction and Overpass Tool, access to satellite data (e.g., Sentinel-5P, EarthCARE), DOI self-assignment for ground-based datasets, and dedicated support for the EarthCARE user community. This tender addresses the next phase of the EVDC's evolution: EVDC Nova. This initiative will establish the foundations for a robust, operational multi-mission platform while ensuring the complete continuity of existing services

title: DISTRIBUTED TEMPERATURE AND STRAIN USING FIBRE OPTICS FOR THE CHARACTERISATION OF LARGE ANTENNA STRUCTURES - EXPRO PLUS
description: Large spaceborne antennas are increasingly required to provide large apertures while meeting stringent mass, dimensional stability and RF performance requirements. Examples include large active phased-array SAR antennas, reflectarrays and deployable reflector antennas. Thermally induced distortions, mechanical loads, deployment effects and long-term structural variations can result in changesof the antenna geometry which may affect the antenna RF characteristics.The knowledge of the actual antenna geometry and its evolution in orbit can therefore provide valuable information for the characterisation and prediction of antenna performance. Conventional temperature sensors provide measurements at discrete locations and do not directly provide information on structural strain or deformation. Similarly, direct geometrical metrology of large antenna structures may require dedicated instrumentation and may be difficult to implement in orbit.Fibre-optic sensing technologies offer the possibility of obtaining quasi-distributed (e.g. Fibre BraggGratings, Fabry-Perot)  and distributed (e.g. Rayleigh, Brillouin and Raman scattering) measurements over large structures with lowsensor mass and limited electrical harnessing. However, their application to large spaceborne antenna structures requires addressing several aspects, including temperature-strain discrimination, sensor integration and routing, spatial resolution, environmental compatibility and reconstruction of the structural deformation from the measured quantities.Previous work has demonstrated the use of fibre-optic strain measurements for shape reconstruction of large and deployable structures and antenna elements. In parallel, experience from large SAR antennas, such as Sentinel-1 and ROSE-L, shows the importance of accurate antenna-pattern knowledge and of accounting for antenna-pattern variations in instrument calibration and data processing.The present activity aims at connecting these two areas by investigating whether distributed/quasi-distributed fibre-optic measurements can provide sufficiently accurate knowledge of the thermomechanical state and deformation of a large antenna structure to support antenna characterisation and, potentially,antenna-pattern prediction or correction.The objective of this activity is to investigate, develop and experimentally validate afibre-optic sensing system for distributed temperature and strain monitoring of large spaceborne antenna structures.The activity shallassess fibre-optic sensing techniques capable of providing distributed measurements of temperature and mechanical strain and shall investigate methods for separating the two measurands.Methods to reconstruct the thermomechanical deformation of the antenna structure from the fibre-optic measurements shall be developed and validated. The impact of the reconstructed structural deformationontheantenna RF performance shall be assessed, including the feasibility of using the reconstructed structural state for antenna-patternprediction and compensation.A representative breadboard shall be designed, manufactured and tested under representative mechanical and thermal loading conditions.

title: END-TO-END DEMONSTRATOR RADAR FOR SPACE OBJECT DETECTION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop and validate an end-to-end demonstrator of a multistatic radar system for space object detection and tracking using cooperative and non-cooperative signals from diverse satellites. The activity evaluates the integration within NewSpace LEO constellations to support advanced surveillance, monitoring, and situational awareness services.Description:  The activity focuses on the development and validation of a complete end-to-end testbed demonstrator for multistatic radar object detection. The system shall operate by receiving and processing reflected signals from multiple satellites, regardless of whether they are designed forcooperative use (e.g. hosted beacons or known signal providers) or non cooperative (e.g. opportunistic use of signals transmitted for other purposes). The aim is to build a prototype capable of operating in representative environments, addressing the practical implementation of hardware and software elements, as well as system integration within NewSpace LEO constellations.  The system designed in this activity focuses on detecting, localizing, and tracking space objects through the reception and processing of reflected signals. Theactivity targets to validate detection performance in controlled settings, assess spatial coverage and scalability, and propose strategies for real-world deployment. A key objective is to enable seamless integration into existing or planned LEO constellations viaflexible architectures, such as hosted payloads or onboard processing modules. The use of a multilayer sensing approach will also be evaluated. The results of this activity aims to contribute to space capabilities in Space Situational Awareness (SSA) and Space Traffic Management (STM), Resilience and Security of Space Assets. The system developed in this activity shall be designed to detectand correlate both direct and reflected signals, supported by the development of advanced algorithms for object detection, tracking,and clutter suppression. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Provide a comprehensive state-of-the-artand feasibility baseline to drive the design of the radar demonstrator architecture. - - - - Provide a complete end-to-end systemarchitecture specification and a technical reference model for demonstrator implementation. Develop a modular, end-to-end software simulator thatmodels the transmission processing chain, signal-object interaction, and receiver-side processing. Develop the functional breadboardimplementations of both the transmitter and receiver chains. Execute a controlled environment validation of thebreadboards and provide experimental validation results. Deliverables: Breadboard, Prototype, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTPWork Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating stateswill be known at tender issue.

title: S3-CL-03 ERASE PHASE A ACTIVE DEBRIS REMOVAL MISSION FOR LARGE UNPREPARED LEO PLATFORMS - EXPRO+
description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry.  The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the  Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028
